title: The World of Work: Labour Laws, Unemployment and Entrepreneurship
summary: Workers' rights and responsibilities under South African labour laws, employment contracts, causes and effects of unemployment, and entrepreneurship and self-employment as alternatives.

rows: Maximum 45 ordinary hours a week; overtime pay; annual, sick, maternity and family-responsibility leave; written particulars of employment
Right to join a trade union and strike; protection against unfair dismissal; the CCMA resolves disputes
Prohibits unfair discrimination; affirmative action for designated groups
A legal minimum hourly wage for most workers
UIF benefits for those who lose their jobs or go on maternity leave

notes.text: An **employment contract** sets out the job, pay, hours, leave and notice period. Employees have **responsibilities** too: arrive on time, work honestly and safely, follow reasonable instructions and respect colleagues.

items: **Causes**: slow economic growth, a mismatch between skills and available jobs, low education levels, automation, and rapid population growth.
**Effects**: poverty, crime, poor mental health, social unrest and lost tax income.
South Africa's youth unemployment rate is among the highest in the world.

notes.text: An **entrepreneur** identifies an opportunity, takes a risk and starts a business. Small businesses create many jobs in South Africa.

items: **Qualities**: creativity, persistence, willingness to take calculated risks, good financial management, networking.
**Support**: the National Youth Development Agency (NYDA), SEDFA (Small Enterprise Development and Finance Agency) and business incubators.
**Steps**: identify a need, research the market, write a business plan, find funding, register the business (with CIPC and SARS), start small and grow.

notes.label: Volunteering and skills
notes.text: Volunteering, internships and short courses build experience and contacts, which improve chances of employment.
